title: Edit Block Folders in the Modular Configurator Window
content: ### **Objective** Edit Block folders at your convenience to organize Blocks in the folders. ** Location** Vertical Menu Tab on the Left ▶ Modular Configurator ▶ (Select) **Block Folder** ** Operation** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Vertical Menu Tab on the Left ▶ Modular Configurator ▶ (Select) **Block Folder** → All Blocks in the selected Block folder appears in the Modular Configurator. 2. Select the ![edit_configurator.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115026695168/edit_configurator.png) **Edit** button. → **Show** icons appear on every Garment thumbnails. 3. Select a Modular Structure file that you want to organize first. → All Blocks compatible with the selected Module Structure are now being displayed. 4. Click on the **Display** icon to either display or hide the Garments or Blocks → Hidden Garments or Blocks appear in lighter shade and the displayed Garments or Blocks appear in brighter shade. 5. Click on the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005619027/______.PNG) **Save** button to save in the configuration file in the same folder as the Block. 6. When editing is done, select the ![____3.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115026695328/____3.png) **Exit** button. → The Blocks appear in the Modular Configurator accordingly. **※ Note: ** * It is able to tie the Modular configuration files as a group by adding a group in the Editor Mode when needing a category that is above all the Modular configuration files. * Unlikely to the Blocks, one Modular configuration file can only be included in one group.

title: [Property] 3D Seamline
content: ### **Objective** Adjust **Intensity** and **Thickness** of 3D seamlines to render a realistic Garment. ** Location ** Main Menu ▶ Sewing ▶ **Edit Sewing ** 3D/2D Toolbar ▶ ![edit_sewing.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024256947/edit_sewing.png) **Edit Sewing** ** Operation ** 1. Select the tool/menu indicated in Location. 2. Select a Sewing Line. → Properties of the Sewing Line appears in the Property Editor. 3. Adjust the settings below as needed: **Option** | **Description** ---|--- [**Normal Map**](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000447607) **(ver 5.2)** | Select an image to be used as the Normal Map. **Intensity (%)** | Adjust the intensity of the Normal Map applied to the seamline. **Thickness** | Adjust the thickness of the Normal Map applied to the seamline.

title: Layer
content: **List of Contents** Layer Set Layer **Layer** \- Set the order of Layers to easily simulate layered 3D Garments. \- Navigate to the Property Editor ▶ Simulation Properties ▶ **Layer.** ** ****Set Layer** \- Using the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022754007/mceclip0.png) **Transform Pattern** tool, select the Pattern to be edited. \- Navigate to the Property Editor ▶ Simulation Properties ▶ **Layer.** \- Type in the value for the Layer option. Assign the greater value to the Patterns layered outwards. \- When the Layer value is assigned, the selected Patterns will be highlighted in neon green. \- Simulate to apply the setting. When Garments are completely simulated, reflecting the Layer setting, turn off the Simulation and reset Layer values of all Patterns to 0. \- When Layer values is 0, Patterns are simulated according to the order placed in the 3D window. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide on how to set and manage layer values for 3D garment simulation using the Layer Set feature in the Property Editor.

title: Subsurface Scattering Material
content: **Objective** Realistically express human skin. Subsurface Scattering Material penetrates and scatters under the objects' surface. Utilize the material to illustrate leaves, fruit, candles and more. Application results are only be viewed in the [Render ](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115014784747-Run-V-Ray-Render)window. [Watch Tutorial Video](https://youtu.be/myqp2Li8FiI) **Location** Fabric Property Editor ▶ Material ▶ Type ▶ **Skin (Render Only)** ** Operation** 1. Select the menu/tool indicated.** ****** 2. Refer to the table below to edit the properties. **Properties** | **Description** ---|--- **Mix** | Adjust the value of Subsurface Scattering (in which light is scattered by penetrating objects). If the value is 0, the material is not applied and is reflected only on the surface of the object. If the value is 1, it is applied to the maximum extent and does not reflect on the surface of the object. **Mix Map**(ver 7.1) | Apply a Mix Map to partially apply the amount of subsurface scattering. **Density Scale** | Adjust the size property of an object to adjust the extent to which SSS is applied. The smaller the value, the wider the SSS coverage. **※ Note:** The Density Scale is applied by multiplying/sharing of each layer radius value, so adjust only the size to which SSS is applied while maintaining the radius ratio between the three layers. **Shallow / Medium / Deep ** | Adjust the properties of the three layers of subsurface scattering to express composite materials. Color | Set the color of the light to be scattered. Color Map | Use a map to express the desired color in the desired area. Weight | The weight of the layer sets the intensity of the color and map of the layer that is set against the other layer. If the value is 1, it has the highest weight. Radius | Set the radius in which each layer scatters inside the surface of the object. 3. Start the [Render](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/ko/articles/115014784747-V-Ray-%EB%A0%8C%EB%8D%94-%EC%8B%A4%ED%96%89) window. → Subsurface Scattering Material materials are applied. **※ Note:** When two or more meshes are overlapped, SSS materials can appear abnormally. Therefore, take the overlapped meshes off each other using other 3D programs, or import the meshes separately and apply SSS materials. ![mceclip0.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360097836353/mceclip0.png)
content_description: This web page provides detailed guidance on using Subsurface Scattering Material to realistically depict human skin and other organic materials in 3D rendering applications.

title: How to Fix the Error using Intel Graphics Card
content: **List of Contents** Case 1 Case 2 (If the error is not resolved by Case 1) Objective Learn how to resolve launching error using Intel HD Graphics. Operation Since this crashing is due to a Graphic driver which is automatically updated by Microsoft Windows, please re-install the Intel graphics driver after deactivating "Windows Automatic Updates". Case 1 1. Please input "gpedit.msc" on Search tool and execute it. 2. Local Group Policy Editor ▶ Computer Configuration ▶ Administrative Templates ▶ Windows Components ▶ Windows Updates ▶ activate "Do not include drivers with Windows Update" ![image_1_1.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360003369948/image_1_1.png)**※ Note:** The option may not appear in the Window versions below. In this case, External Graphics card should be used. (Please refer to [Computer Specification](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000307168-Computer-Specifications)) Windows 7 Home Edition / Windows 10 Home Edition 3. Device Manager ▶ Display Adapters ▶ Intel(R) HD Graphic ▶ Uninstall the device and driver software ▶ Reboot Windows ![image_2_1.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360003447047/image_2_1.png) 4. Enter [Intel Support Page](https://www.intel.com/content/www/us/en/support/intel-driver-support-assistant.html) and download and install the program of Intel® Driver & Support Assistant. 5. Start scanning the driver. 6. Download and Reinstall the driver of Intel(R) HD Graphics. 7. Verify the "23.20.16.4901" version is installed correctly.![image_3.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360003369968/image_3.png) 8. Please reboot Windows. 9. If the Error is not resolved with Case 1, please proceed Case 2 below. **Case 2** If the Error is not resolved with Case 1, please proceed Case 2. 1. Please enter [Intel® Graphics Driver for Windows*](https://downloadcenter.intel.com/download/27412/Graphics-Intel-Graphics-Driver-for-Windows-15-60-?wapkw=hd+graphic) and Download & Install the driver. 2. Approve overwrite to the previous version during Installation. ![image_3_1.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360003369988/image_3_1.png) Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This webpage provides a step-by-step guide to resolving launching errors related to Intel HD Graphics by reinstalling the graphics driver and adjusting Windows update settings.

title: Polygon
content: **List of Contents** Polygon Create Polygon Create Polygon with Curves Create Polygon with Specific Values Create Points in Guidelines Cancel the Last Action Cancel All Actions **Polygon** \- Create Polygon Patterns in the 2D window. \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022648248/mceclip0.png) **Polygon** tool from the 2D toolbar. \- Or, navigate to the Main Menu and select 2D Pattern ▶ Create ▶ **Polygon.** ** Create Polygon** \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022648248/mceclip0.png) **Polygon** tool and click on the 2D window to draw desired shape of Polygon. \- Click the start point again to complete the Pattern. **Create Polygon with Curves** \- Hold down the Ctrl key while clicking the 2D window to create curves with the free curve point. \- Or, click and drag the mouse while adding a point on the 2D window to create curves with AI Bezier handles. **Create Polygon with Specific Values** \- Click and then right click on the 2D window to access the Create Polygon window. \- Type in the desired value to Length. **Create Points in Guidelines** \- Hold down the Shift key on the keyboard to add points in a straight line or a diagonal line. **Cancel the Last Action** \- While creating the Polygon Pattern, hit the Delete key on the keyboard to cancel the last action. **Cancel All Actions** \- While creating the Polygon Pattern, hit the Esc or Ctrl+Z keys on the keyboard to cancel all actions. title: Curved Side Geometry
content: ### **Objective** Apply and adjust curvature on edges of Patterns for more natural and realistic look (ver2.2.0). **Location** 2D Toolbar ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005541708/Toolbar_2D_Pattern_Transform.png) **Transform Pattern** / ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005494467/Toolbar_2D_Pattern_Edit.png) **Edit Pattern** **Operation** 1. Firstly, change the 3D Garment rendering style to **Thick Textured Surface** in the 3D window. 2. Follow the indicated guideline below: 2D Toolbar **▶![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005541708/Toolbar_2D_Pattern_Transform.png) Transform Pattern** **/![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005494467/Toolbar_2D_Pattern_Edit.png) Edit Pattern**** ** 3. [Load an OBJ](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000494107). 2. Follow the indicated guideline below: Load OBJ as Trim ▶ ![scale_gizmo.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024298848/scale_gizmo.png) **Scale** → The **Scale Gizmo** appears. 3. Click and drag on the x,y, or z-axis to transform the OBJ. **Axis** | **Description** ---|--- **X-Axis** | The red axis of the Gizmo. Click and drag the x-axis to transform the OBJ trim along its x-axis. **Y-Axis** | The yellow-green axis of the Gizmo. Click and drag the y-axis to transform the OBJ trim along its y-axis. **Z-Axis** | The blue axis of the Gizmo. Click and drag the z-axis to transform the OBJ along its z-axis. **Square** | The yellow square located in the center of the **Scale Gizmo**. Click and drag the square to transform the OBJ trim, while maintaining its x, y, and z ratio. → The OBJ is transformed. 4. When the OBJ transformation is complete, click the ![scale_gizmo.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024298848/scale_gizmo.png) **Scale** button again. → The **Gizmo** used for moving and rotating OBJs appears. **Via the Property Editor ** 1. [Load an OBJ](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000494107). 2. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 3D Garment ▶ **Select/Move ** 3D Toolbar**▶![Toolbar_3D_Select_Move.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024215067/Toolbar_3D_Select_Move.png) Select/Move ** 3. Select the OBJ to be transformed. → The properties of the OBJ appear in the Property Editor. 4. Find the **Scale** option. 5. Enter the desired value for below options. **Option** | **Description** ---|--- **X-Axis** | Enter the desired x-axis value. **Y-Axis** | Enter the desired y-axis value. **Z-Axis** | Enter the desired z-axis value. **Maintain Ratio** | Toggle this option on to adjust an OBJ while maintaining its x, y, and z ratio. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides step-by-step instructions for transforming OBJ files using both the Scale Gizmo and the Property Editor in CLO 3D.

title: Strengthen
content: **List of Contents** Strengthen Result of Strengthen **Strengthen** \- Temporarily harden Patterns while simulating the 3D Garment. \- Strengthen when folding or straightening Patterns in the 3D window. \- Use the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022739767/mceclip0.png) **Transform Pattern** tool to select patterns, right click, and select **Strengthen. ** Windows Shortcut: Ctrl + H Mac Shortcut: Ctrl + L (ver5.0.0)** ** ** Result of Strengthen** \- When the Patterns are strengthened properly, they turn orange. \- The Patterns will temporarily gain strength and express clean folds where fold angles are applied. \- To unstrengthen the Pattern, use the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022739767/mceclip0.png) **Transform Pattern** tool to select Pattern, right click, and select **Unstrengthen. ** Windows Shortcut: Ctrl + H Mac Shortcut: Ctrl + L (ver5.0.0) Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides a concise guide on how to strengthen and unstrengthen patterns in a 3D garment simulation using specific tools and shortcuts.

title: Video Capture 3D Garment (Turntable)
content: **List of Contents** Record Quit **Objective** Easily record 3D garments with Turntable, utilize it when communicating. ** Location** **Record** Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Video Capture ▶ **Turntable** **Quit** X button on the top-right corner of Turntable dialogue ▶ **X Button** ** Operation** **Record** 1. Select the tool/menu indicated in Location. → Turntable dialogue window appears at the bottom-right corner. 2. Set options as needed and start recording. ** Video Size ** | Adjust the orientation, width and height of the turntable video window. ---|--- ** Options ** | Rotation Axis (ver 6.1) | Set the rotation axis of a Turntable video. Auto | The axis is set to the center of the garment and avatar in the 3D window. Center (0.0) | The axis is set to the center (0.0) in the 3D window. Custom | Enter the desired value of the X and Z-axis to set the desired axis. Direction | Set the direction (clockwise/ counter-clockwise) of the turntable. Duration | Set the duration of the turntable video. Minimum of 1 second and a maximum of 60 seconds. Save HTML File | The turntable is saved as HTML. ** Video Codec ** | Set the codec to use when recording video. **※ Note: **it is available to save MP4/AVI for Windows and MOV files for MAC without installing a separate codec. ** Record ** | ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005767708/capture_01rec_on.png) / ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005767728/capture_01rec_refresh_on.png) | Start or delete the recording and return to the initial state. **Quit** 1. Select the tool/menu indicated in Location. →**** Recording stops and the dialogue window disappears. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides a concise guide for users on how to efficiently record 3D garments using a Turntable, enhancing communication and presentation of their designs.

title: [2D Tool] M:N Free Sewing
content: **Objective** Freely establish Sewing Lines on Pattern outlines and Internal Shapes/Lines to sew multiple Patterns (M) to multiple Patterns (N) at once. ** Location** Main Menu ▶ Sewing ▶ **M:N Free Sewing** 2D Toolbar ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005448927/M_N________.png) **M:N Free Sewing** **※ Note:** Hold down the **Free Sewing** tool for a while to access the **M:N Free Sewing** Tool. ** Operation** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Sewing ▶ **M:N Free Sewing** 2D Toolbar ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005448927/M_N________.png) **M:N Free Sewing** 2. Establish Free Sewing Lines on multiple Patterns, which are considered as M Patterns. 3. Hit the Enter key on the keyboard to complete. → The Sewing Lines appear in neon color. 4. While being mindful of Directional Notches, establish Sewing Lines on Patterns which are sewn to M Patterns. Hit the Enter key on the keyboard to complete M:N Sewing Lines. → All Sewing Lines no longer appear in neon color. **※ Note:** * While establishing the Sewing Lines, hit the Delete key on the keyboard to cancel the last action or hit the Esc key on the keyboard to cancel all actions. * While establishing M:N sewing lines, if you click on an inappropriate segment, the segment appears in red and the Sewing Line cannot be applied. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: The **M:N Free Sewing** page provides users with the tools and guidelines to efficiently create and manage sewing lines across multiple patterns simultaneously in a user-friendly interface.

title: Change Length
content: **Objective** Type in the segment length and edit Pattern. **Location** Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ **Edit Pattern** 2D Toolbar ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115001101227/2.png) **Edit Pattern** ** ****Operation** 1. Select the tool/menu indicated in Location 2. Right-click on the segment to be adjusted to access the pop-up menu. Then, select **Change Length.** → The Change Length window appears. 3. Set each option and click the **OK **button. **Length** | Enter the length of the segment to change. ---|--- **Direction** | Set the direction to change the length. **Lock Curve Points** | If a line connected to the selected line is a curve, the curve point is moved according to the changed length. To move only straight point, click this option. → The segment length is changed accordingly. ※ Note: When clicking continuous line segements, it is recognized as a single segment and change in length (ver 7.1)
content_description: The purpose of this web page is to guide users through the process of editing segment lengths in a 2D pattern using the Edit Pattern tool.

title: Merge Points on Internal Lines
content: **List of Contents** Join Overlapping Points Merge to Point Merge to Average Intersect & Merge **Objective** Join or merge two open points on Internal Lines. **※ Note: **When a point on the Internal Line is open, it is hollow, whereas when a point on the Internal Line is closed, it is filled. ** Location** Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ **Transform Pattern** / **Edit Pattern** 2D Toolbar ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115001094287/1.png) **Transform Pattern** / ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115001141208/2.png) **Edit Pattern** ** Operation** **Join Overlapping Points** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ **Transform Pattern** / **Edit Pattern** 2D Toolbar ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115001094287/1.png) **Transform Pattern** / ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115001141208/2.png) **Edit Pattern** 2. Select overlapping points and right click to access the pop-up menu. Then, select **Join Overlapping Points**. → Two overlapping points are joined and closed. **Merge to Point** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ **Edit Pattern** 2D Toolbar ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115001141208/2.png) **Edit Pattern** 2. Select two points on Internal Lines to be merged. 3. Right click on the point which the other point should be merged to. When the pop-up menu appears, select **Merge to Point**. → The point is merged to the right-clicked point. **Merge to Average** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ **Edit Pattern** 2D Toolbar ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115001141208/2.png) **Edit Pattern** 2. Select two points on the Internal Lines to be merged. Then, right click on either point to access the pop-up menu and select **Merge to Average**. → The selected points are merged to their average point. **Intersect & Merge** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ **Edit Pattern** 2D Toolbar ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115001141208/2.png) **Edit Pattern** 2. Select two points to be merged. 3. Right click on the points to access the pop-up menu and select **Intersect & Merge**. → The selected points are shortened or extended maintaining their current slope and are merged where they intersect. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This webpage provides a step-by-step guide on how to join or merge open points on Internal Lines in 2D pattern editing, ensuring accurate transformations in your designs.
